events.title: Mamluks defeat the Mongols at Ain Jalut
events.description: In Palestine, an Egyptian Mamluk army dealt the Mongol Empire one of its first major battlefield defeats. The Mongols had until then seemed unstoppable in their westward advance.
events.significance: The victory halted Mongol expansion into the Middle East and North Africa, and it preserved Egypt as a center of Islamic power.

events.title: Death of Oliver Cromwell
events.description: Oliver Cromwell, who had ruled England as Lord Protector since the abolition of the monarchy, died. His son Richard succeeded him.
events.significance: Richard proved unable to hold power, and the Protectorate soon collapsed. This paved the way for the restoration of the monarchy in 1660.

events.title: Treaty of Paris ends the American Revolutionary War
events.description: Representatives of Great Britain and the United States signed the treaty in Paris. Britain formally recognized American independence.
events.significance: The treaty set the borders of the new nation and marked the birth of the United States as a sovereign country.

events.title: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
events.description: Returning from holiday, Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold had killed bacteria in one of his lab dishes. The mold was the source of what became penicillin.
events.significance: Penicillin became the first widely used antibiotic and has saved countless lives, ushering in the modern era of medicine.

events.title: Britain and France declare war on Germany
events.description: Two days after Germany invaded Poland, Britain and France declared war on Germany. Their declarations turned the invasion into a wider European conflict.
events.significance: This marked the start of World War II in Europe, a conflict that reshaped the world order and lasted six years.
